solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Where trial is broadcast and heard

indicators.note: something broadcast is sent out as sound, so we take the word as spoken

parts.note: a trial is held in a court; said in a British accent that drops the R, it gives a word spelt differently

explanation.surface: A court case being aired on radio or television for all to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone only works in accents that drop the R: COURT and CAUGHT are identical in standard British English.
explanation.definitionFit: To have caught what someone said is to have heard it.

clue.text: Group of commuters race after Mark cycling

indicators.note: the letters go round, the first moving to the back

parts.note: SCAR (mark) with its first letter moved to the end
to hare is to race along

explanation.surface: A cycle race involving a rider called Mark, with commuters watching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name in the surface; here it is a scar.
explanation.definitionFit: A carshare is an arrangement where several commuters travel in one car.

clue.text: Rounded section of Sumatran lumpfish is bony?

indicators.note: turned round, so the hidden letters read backwards
the answer is a section cut from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A zoological note that the curved part of a fish from Sumatra is bony.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a loose definition: ULNAR means relating to the ulna, a bone of the forearm, so it is 'bony' only in a narrow sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulnar describes the ulna, one of the two bones of the forearm.

clue.text: Suffers fools

definitions.meaning: to suffer from an illness is to have it, as in 'he ___ flu'
you've been had = you've been fooled

explanation.surface: A terse remark that someone puts up with idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'suffers fools' as the idiom about tolerating idiots; both words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: One 'has' an illness and one can 'have' someone on, meaning trick them.

clue.text: Haul iron spades into street fight

explanation.surface: Someone hauling iron spades into a brawl in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Street fight' looks like the whole definition, but 'street' is ST, which wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A slugfest is a fight where both sides trade heavy blows.

clue.text: Eating tons, managed personal disappointment

indicators.note: what is eaten ends up inside the eater

explanation.surface: Someone ate tons of food and felt personally disappointed afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The containment makes LETD first; OWN then follows. The comma is only punctuation for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something that lets you down is a disappointment.

clue.text: Men anger god arousing figure in bed?

indicators.note: to arouse is to stir up, and stirred-up letters lose their order

explanation.surface: Men enraging a deity by stirring up a figure in bed, with a racy hint.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, not a bedroom one; the question mark marks that twist.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden gnome is a small figure that sits in a flower bed.

clue.text: Sociable former footballer stops not drinking

definitions.note: Extrovert here is the adjective, matching 'Sociable'.

parts.note: a player for a club called Rovers, such as Bristol Rovers

explanation.surface: A friendly ex-footballer who has given up alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: Many English football clubs are called Rovers, so a ROVER is a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: Extrovert used as an adjective means outgoing and sociable.

clue.text: Nearly shot island bird

indicators.note: not quite all of the word: its last letter goes

parts.note: TURN (a shot, a go) without its last letter
a key is a small low island, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: A bird on an island that was almost shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire, but it means a go or attempt, as in 'have a shot'. KEY for island is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A general term for a specific: the turkey is one kind of bird.

clue.text: Measure sides as a whole?

definitions.meaning: an old unit of distance, about three miles
all the teams in a competition together

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether to measure the sides of something all at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sides' are sports teams, not the edges of a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an old measure of distance and also the full set of teams in a competition.

clue.text: Missing start, stadium track is making a comeback

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: the trail an animal leaves, which hounds track

explanation.surface: A stadium's running track is being revived after a false start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Track' looks like the running track; here it is a scent trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn, becoming active again.

clue.text: Blade whirling either way

indicators.note: the answer reads the same in either direction

explanation.surface: A blade spinning in both directions.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no fodder: the definition gives the word and 'either way' confirms it reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the spinning blade assembly of a helicopter or turbine.

clue.text: Misbehaving bachelor admitted to perfect pattern

parts.note: to hone a skill is to perfect it; the outer piece

explanation.surface: A badly behaved bachelor accepted into an ideal plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfect' looks like an adjective in the surface; it is the verb, to hone, split round the inserted letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Herringbone is a zigzag pattern used in fabrics and brickwork.

clue.text: Anger happening to bore people

parts.note: to bore a hole is to dig

explanation.surface: Anger arising from being bored by people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like a tedious person; it is the verb, to drill.
explanation.definitionFit: A near synonym: indignation is the particular anger felt at unfair treatment.

clue.text: Dictator's due tribute?

indicators.note: a dictator here is someone dictating aloud, so the word is spoken

parts.note: what is due is owed; said aloud, that word is a short poem

explanation.surface: A dictator expecting the praise he thinks he deserves.
explanation.walkthrough: The dictator is not a tyrant but someone dictating: what they say is heard, not seen.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a poem written in praise of someone, a tribute.

clue.text: Lie about uranium remnants

definitions.note: Residue is singular, but it is a mass noun covering whatever remnants are left.

parts.note: to lie somewhere is to reside there; the outer piece

explanation.surface: A cover-up about leftover nuclear material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lie' suggests a falsehood; it means to be situated, to reside.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains after the rest is gone.

clue.text: Change to hammers automated building

indicators.note: alter the order of the letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to switch to hammers in some construction work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' reads as the imperative in the surface, and 'to hammers' as its target; all nine letters of 'to hammers' are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart home has its lights, heating and so on controlled automatically.

clue.text: Piece retreating to capture another?

definitions.note: 'Another' stands for another piece, following on from the first word; a nugget is a piece of gold.

parts.note: 'piece' is gangster slang for a gun
to get someone is to capture them

explanation.surface: A chess piece falling back in order to take another piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess picture hides both meanings of piece: a gun in the wordplay, and 'another' piece, a nugget, as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a piece, typically a lump of gold.

clue.text: Person demonstrating regret to billions when overthrown

indicators.note: turned over, so the whole string reads backwards

explanation.surface: A person showing remorse to billions of people after being ousted from power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overthrown' suggests a toppled ruler; it turns the whole string over. A saboteur here is a protester, such as a hunt saboteur who disrupts fox hunts.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately disrupts things, often as a form of protest.

clue.text: Fare from Scotland has bags regularly going astray

indicators.note: to bag something is to capture it, so HAS holds the rest

parts.note: used as itself, the outer piece

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken
the letters wander out of order

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of GoInG

explanation.surface: Someone's luggage keeps getting lost on a trip to Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has bags' reads like owning luggage; 'bags' is really the container instruction for HAS. Haggis is Scotland's national dish of spiced offal cooked in a sheep's stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggis is a traditional Scottish food.

clue.text: Old brass boat capsized under fire

indicators.note: turned upside down, so in a down clue TUB reads upwards

parts.note: to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: An old brass-bound boat overturned while under fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' suggests guns; it means dismiss. 'Old brass' is the definition, an early instrument, not old metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is the Renaissance ancestor of the trombone, a brass instrument.

clue.text: Country bread keeps American in California

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it

parts.note: US state abbreviation, the outermost piece

explanation.surface: A loaf of country bread kept by an American living in California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country bread' reads as rustic bread, but 'Country' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Croatia is one country, on the Adriatic coast of Europe.

clue.text: Cold capital by peak

parts.note: c = cold, as on a tap
x = by, the multiplication sign, as in 3 x 4

explanation.surface: A chilly capital city beside a mountain peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like a positional link; it is the times sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the climax of a story or career is its peak, the high point.

clue.text: Beginners in croquet often take this stick

indicators.note: the first letters of the next words

parts.note: first letters of Croquet and Often
what you say handing something over: 'here, take this'

explanation.surface: Novice croquet players are often handed this mallet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like the croquet mallet; it is a verb, to cling together.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: things that cohere hold or stick together.

clue.text: Plump duck served with pint

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, O

explanation.surface: A fat duck served alongside a pint of beer in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump' looks like an adjective describing the duck; it is the verb, as in to plump for something.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to 'plump for' something means to choose it, which is what opting does.

clue.text: Bridge pile replaced earlier chain

indicators.note: the letters are placed afresh, in a new order

parts.note: an arch spans a gap, like a bridge

explanation.surface: A bridge support pile that was swapped out for an earlier chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chain' suggests metal links, but the definition is a chain of islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: islands strung out in a line form a chain, and such a group is an archipelago.

clue.text: A US campus meets variable goodwill

parts.note: algebra uses x, y and z as variables

explanation.surface: An American university welcoming changeable goodwill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variable' looks like an adjective meaning changeable; it is the noun, an algebra letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Amity is friendship, goodwill between people.

clue.text: Ice is one ingredient of the mojito

definitions.note: The definition is by example: an ice cube is one of the many emoji.

indicators.note: the answer is contained in the words that follow

explanation.surface: Ice is one of the components of a mojito cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true of the cocktail; the definition is that ice is one emoji, a picture character on a phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Emojis include an ice cube among their little pictures.

clue.text: Produce aisle losing length to stock new sauce

indicators.note: a word that loses something no longer has it, so AISLE lets its L go

parts.note: to bear fruit is to produce it

explanation.surface: A supermarket's produce aisle gets shorter to make room for a new sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce aisle' is the fruit and vegetable section; here 'Produce' is the verb, to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Béarnaise is a rich sauce of butter, egg yolk and tarragon.

clue.text: Queue up endlessly for nothing

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading upwards reverses the letters
the last letter is removed

parts.note: a queue is a line of people

explanation.surface: Queueing up forever and getting nothing for it.
explanation.walkthrough: LINE loses its end to give LIN, and 'up' turns that round. 'Queue up' reads as one phrase in the surface, but 'up' is the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, common in sports scores: nil is nothing, zero.

clue.text: Shaping of tiny tree which never ends

definitions.note: The definition is a descriptive phrase, 'that which never ends', standing for a noun.

indicators.note: giving the letters a new shape

explanation.surface: Shaping a bonsai, a tiny tree, is a job that is never finished.
explanation.walkthrough: A bonsai is pruned for decades, so the surface's endless shaping is true to life.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is time without end.

clue.text: Tip to finish level one on a video game?

indicators.note: take the finishing letter of 'Tip'

explanation.surface: A gaming tip for completing level one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Level one' reads as the first stage of a game, but 'one' belongs to the definition: the one on the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who plays, or is on, a video game.
